# Golden saves corpus

One world-shaped JSON payload per historical save schema: `v0.json` … `v{SAVE_SCHEMA_VERSION}.json`.

**Backward compatibility is a hard product guarantee.** A player who last opened the game on any
past version must be able to load their career after an update. `tests/goldenSaves.test.ts` runs
every fixture here through `migrateSave` and asserts it upgrades cleanly to the current schema.

## The rule (enforced by the test)

- There must be exactly one fixture for **every** version from `v0` to the current
  `SAVE_SCHEMA_VERSION` (from `src/engine/world.ts`).
- Bumping `SAVE_SCHEMA_VERSION` therefore **fails the suite until a new `vN.json` is added** — the
  guard forces you to capture a representative save of the shape you just froze.

## How each fixture was reconstructed

Shapes come straight from the append-only history in `src/engine/migrations.ts`:

| file | shape (delta vs the version before) |
| ---- | ----------------------------------- |
| v0 | pre-release dev save: no `schemaVersion`, no `fundsCents`, flat `log` strings |
| v1 | `+schemaVersion +fundsCents +log` |
| v2 | `+profile` (no `playStyle`) |
| v3 | profile `+playStyle` |
| v4 | `+plan` (weekly time split) |
| v5 | `+careerId` (career profiles) |
| v6 | living world: `+cohort +results +season +entries +events +nextEventId +kidRank`, `log` dropped |
| v7 | profile `+kidLastName`, world `+prevKidRank` |
| v8 | world `+pendingTournament` (tournament-reveal flow; `null` when no reveal is in progress) |
| v9 | profile `+birthMonth` (1-12; relative-age-effect groundwork, round-3 QA item 16 / round-6) |
| v10 | world `+bestFinishByTier +lastSeasonSummary +seasonWins +seasonLosses` (Home season strip + SeasonSummaryDialog) |
| v11 | world `+financeWeeks` (per-week/per-category finance ledger; feeds the Money breakdown past the 60-event cap) |
| v12 | world `+condition +injury +injuryHistory +physioActive` (Season-Life availability gate; injury/physio wired for Slice C, condition drives the fatigue caution) |
| v13 | world `+vacations +practices +recoveryBuff` (season planner: booked family-vacation weeks, booked practice-match weeks, and the carry-over injury-tau buff from a resort/elite package) |
| v14 | world `+seasonHistory` (R10-9: append-only per-season record – year, end rank, points, W-L, funds delta, closing funds, best finish – behind the Stats season-by-season table; `lastSeasonSummary` is overwritten yearly, this list is not) |
| v15 | world `+internationalEntryWeeks` (the ITF annual entry cap: the absolute week of every j30/j60/j300 entry she has made, counted per season against `ECONOMY.entryCap.perYearByAge`. Pre-v15 saves backfill to an empty ledger – nothing in them can reconstruct it, since the kid's result row is award-only) |
| v17 | world `+seasonStartRank` (R12-S1: her dense rank as she ENTERED the season in progress, captured at the tick into the season's first week. It is not derivable at wrap-up time – the 52-week prune has removed every result behind it by then, which is how the wrap-up came to replay an almost-empty table, tie the whole field on 0 points and report "from #1". Pre-v17 saves backfill to `null`, the "not recorded" value `SeasonSummary.startRank` has always allowed, and capture a real one from the next season boundary) |
| v16 | `seasonHistory` rows `year` → `+seasonIndex` (a season's identity is its 0-based index, never the calendar year of its first Monday – a season is 364 days, so that year repeats at season 5 and the wrap-up's dedup guard silently dropped a whole season's row). The backfill is an exact inversion: the old guard kept the first season to claim a year, so the smallest index yielding it is the one that wrote it) |
| v18 | world `+milestones` (Diary-1 D10: the durable milestone ledger behind the Memory card – first title/final per tier, first international entry, first injury, each season's closing rank, captured at the moment they happen. Pre-v18 saves backfill from surviving evidence: tournament events + the kept `first-title` event + kid result rows for titles/finals, `injuryHistory` for the first injury (onset = week − weeksOut), `seasonHistory` for season ranks, and the earliest surviving j30+ trace for the first international. Earliest evidence wins per identity; history already pruned away is honestly unrecoverable, so a backfilled "first" is the earliest surviving one) |

| v19 | world `+skills +potential` (Phase 4 development: her build stops being re-derived from `seed:kid` on demand and becomes state that moves, under a ceiling rolled once from `seed:potential`. Pre-v19 saves backfill from that same derivation, so a migrated career is byte-identical at the moment it loads and simply starts developing from there) |
| v20 | cohort rows `+ageYears +potential` (the field gets an age and a ceiling – it used to grow ~1.5 a year for ever, so no career could catch it. Backfilled deterministically from the player's seed, with each rival's ceiling measured from where the old unbounded drift left them, so a long-running save keeps the players it earned) |
| v21 | world `+academy` (the academy scholarship: `{level, sinceWeek, seasonIndex, coveredCents}` or `null`. Pre-v21 saves backfill to `null` rather than replaying the reviews they never had – a replay would have to invent the offer, the renewals and the kit grants, or hand her a scholarship she was never told about. The next season boundary reviews her on the year she just played and makes a real offer) |
| v24 | world `+coachOnEventWeeks` (does the coach travel to tournaments? A competition week stops being billed as a coaching week by default – she spends it in a draw, not on his court – and this buys him for those weeks anyway. It moves BOTH the bill and the development rate, because a coach who is not paid for a week is not at that week, which is what keeps it a decision rather than free money. Back-filled **false**, which is the new default and deliberately NOT a preservation of what the save was doing: an existing career was billed every week, so the migration makes its coach cheaper and, on tournament weeks, absent. The owner's framing is that the automatic rule is "competition weeks are not coach weeks", so that is what a migrated career should wake up under – and it is the cheaper direction, which is the safe one to migrate into) |
| v23 | world `+coachId` (a roster coach's id, or `null` for the parent on the court. The roster is a pure derivation of the seed – `engine/coach.ts buildCoachRoster` – so only the id is stored and it resolves for ever without a further migration. The back-fill hires the coach at the rung the career was already being billed at, choosing by style fit and then by price, which is the same rule `openingCoachId` applies to a brand-new career: the save keeps its tier and its development factor and simply gains a name and a face for the money it was already spending) |
| v25 | world `skills` / `potential` `+groundstrokes` (the fifth attribute – damage off the ground, the leg of a point the model never had. Both numbers come off draws APPENDED to the existing `seed:kid` / `seed:potential` sub-streams, so the four attributes a save already holds are byte-identical and no career's build moves. The back-fill is the interesting half: her birth value would open a week-200 career with a fourteen-year-old's forehand and her ceiling would be the mirror mistake, so she is placed at **the same share of the new axis's headroom that she has taken on the other four** – she has been hitting forehands the whole time, the attribute was not modelled but the girl was. This fixture is the real migration's own output on `v24.json`: that career is 33.8% of the way to its ceiling on all four, so its groundstroke lands 33.8% of the way from 51 to 55.6. A fresh career gets `progress = 0`, i.e. exactly `startingSkills`, so a new game and a migrated week-1 game are still the same career) |
| v26 | world `+knock +knockHistory` (W4 – the knock: the ordinary training week's one event. She comes off court sore, and the parent rests it or sends her back out; see `src/engine/knock.ts`. `knock` is the live one – part, the week it arrived, whether it is a part he has pushed through before, and **his answer** – and `knockHistory` is the retired ones, which is what makes the thread accumulate (`pushedParts` reads it to decide which part of her body speaks up next). **Both back-fill EMPTY, and unlike v18's milestones there is nothing to reconstruct**: a knock left no trace an old save could carry – it was never rolled, never logged, never persisted – so there is no earlier evidence to mine. Inventing rows would mean inventing *decisions the player never made*, and since `knockHistory` is precisely the record of his decisions, a fabricated row would hand a career a weak shoulder whose owner never ignored anything. A migrated career therefore wakes up with a clean body and a clean record, and its first knock arrives on its next ordinary training week like any other. Nothing else in the save moves: the two sub-streams (`seed:knock:<week>`, `seed:knockread:<sinceWeek>`) did not exist before, so no existing stream shifts by a draw, and the injury threshold's new post-draw multiply returns exactly 1 while `knock` is null – which it is for every migrated save at the moment it loads. This fixture is the real migration's own output on `v25.json`, the same recipe v25 used on v24) |
| v28 | world `+seasonRecord` (the season W-L, told apart by ladder – `{domestic: {wins, losses}, itf: {wins, losses}}`. The owner, 31.07: «national/international разделить победы и поражения, мне кажется они не должны быть общими». It is a **decomposition** of the two v10 counters and NOT a replacement for them: `matchesEverPlayed` folds `seasonWins + seasonLosses` into the radar's confidence, which is documented as a count that may only ever go UP, so a total that fell would re-thicken the fog on its own. The back-fill is a real **reconstruction**, and exact wherever the event feed still reaches: `finalizeTournament` is the only writer of a `tournament` event, it stamps `finishIdx`, and a finish index over a known draw size IS the match count – `rounds - finishIdx` wins plus, unless she won the thing, exactly one loss. The tier comes off the summary's label prefix through the shared longest-label-first lookup, the same recipe v10 and v18 use. Only the CURRENT season is read, because the counters reset at every wrap-up and an older row is already banked in `seasonHistory`; a save whose feed has pruned past its season start keeps its true total and gets a split accounting for as much of it as the evidence supports, with the remainder attributed to neither ladder because nothing left in the save says which one it was. Same bargain v17 struck for `seasonStartRank`, and it costs at most the tail of one season on one screen. This fixture is the real migration's own output on `v27.json`, the recipe v25 and v26 used) |
| v30 | world `seasonRecord` `+wta` (the adult rungs, task #17). `LadderTrack` went from two members to three, and `seasonRecord` is the only place in a save where that union is a persisted KEY SET rather than something re-derived on the next tick – every other consumer (`kidRankWta`, `prevKidRankWta`, `ladders.wta`) re-folds from the results ledger and therefore needed no migration at all. Without this step a save written before the professional table existed would carry a two-key object into a three-key type and `record[track].wins++` in `finalizeTournament` would throw on `undefined` the first time she won a W15 match. **The back-fill is uniquely EXACT among the ones in this file**: v18 mined surviving evidence and admitted its "firsts" were only the earliest still-visible ones, v28 reconstructed a split and clamped it because the feed had been pruned, v29 refused to guess at all – this one guesses nothing and loses nothing, because W15/W35/W100 did not exist in any shipped build and so no match in any save reaching this line can have been played on the professional table. Zero is not a placeholder for the true value, it IS the true value, and the invariant `seasonRecord` sums to `seasonWins`/`seasonLosses` still holds afterwards. Written defensively (an absent or non-object `seasonRecord` is rebuilt whole) because append-only means a later step must not assume an earlier one's post-condition still reads the way it did the day it was written. This fixture is the real migration's own output on `v29.json`, the recipe every fixture since v25 uses) |
| v22 | profile `coachSetup` → `coachTier` (the coach ladder: `'parent' \| 'hired'` becomes `'self' \| 'budget' \| 'middle' \| 'high' \| 'elite'`. The back-fill is the owner's ruling and deliberately blunt: `hired` → `elite`, `parent` → `self`. It is also what the arithmetic mostly said – the old `hired` band's ~$475/wk midpoint is what the spec prices an Elite coach at, to within $5 – and both mappings are **development-neutral**: `self` carries 0.82, exactly the old `coachParent`, and `elite` carries 1.15, exactly `coachHired`, so no migrated career's growth rate moves. Only its bill does, and the Coach Market ships in the same wave to let it change) |
| v29 | `seasonHistory` rows `+spentCents +earnedCents` (W7 – what each season COST and BROUGHT IN, gross, in positive cents. The owner: «было бы очень интересно где-то хранить всю историю затрат за карьеру по годам в каком-то виде». `fundsDeltaCents` was already there and answers a different question – whether the year ended up or down – which a season of big prize money and bigger bills reports as a shrug. **The migration is a NO-OP and that is the point**: the figures come off `financeWeeks`, which is pruned to a 60-week trailing window, so every season older than ~14 months has had its per-category rows deleted from the save long before this runs, and the only other trace (`lastSeasonSummary`) holds one season and is overwritten yearly. A back-fill would have to invent numbers, and this is the field where an invented number is worst: the whole feature is a parent asking what she has cost, and a fabricated answer to that is a lie with a dollar sign on it. Both fields are OPTIONAL and the reader prints silence for a row without them – the contract `bestFinish` has carried since v14 – so a migrated career shows its old seasons as not recorded and keeps real figures from its next wrap-up. This fixture is the real migration's own output on `v27.json`, the same recipe v25 and v26 used) |
| v31 | world `+trophiesByTier` (the TITLES LEDGER, behind the Trophy Cabinet: `Record<TierId, {titles: number[], finals: number[]}>`, arrays of the absolute WEEKS she won a tier and the weeks she LOST a final at it. Written in `finalizeTournament` beside the v10 `bestFinishByTier` update. **It is a new fact rather than a view of an old one, because nothing already in a save can answer "how many, and when"**: `bestFinishByTier` is a single high-water mark with no week and no count, and it is overwritten the day a silver becomes a gold; `milestones` is firsts-only by identity (`title:<tier>`, so a five-time J30 champion has one row); `results` prunes at 52 weeks and `events` at 400, of which only 60 reach a Snapshot. ⚠ `finals` here means **she LOST the final** – the opposite of `MilestoneType: 'final'`, which a title also captures – because a cabinet counts pieces of silverware and a week produces exactly one; counted the milestone's way the silver plate would light up the first time she WON something. **The back-fill is a deliberate NO-OP, in v29's sense**: the shape is created, the history is not invented. The evidence is pruned away, and the little that survives would give a confident WRONG answer rather than a partial one – reading `milestones` would print "1 J30 title, in 2033" for a five-time champion, a number with a year on it that never happened. v18 could strike that bargain because a memory that starts late is still a memory; a cabinet prints a COUNT, and the count is the whole point. The owner, asked directly: «нас это в данный момент не беспокоит». So a migrated career wakes up with eighteen empty shelves and its next final is the first thing that goes in one. Written defensively (an absent or non-object value is rebuilt whole) for the append-only reason v30 states, and `finalizeTournament` creates a missing tier's row on demand so a tenth rung on `TIER_LADDER` needs no further migration at all. This fixture is the real migration's own output on `v30.json`, the recipe every fixture since v25 uses) |
| v32 | world `+offers` (THE INBOX: every letter this career has been sent – `{id, kind, week, deadlineWeek, terms, state}` plus the two bookkeeping fields a signed deal needs, see `docs/specs/offers-and-the-inbox.md` §2. This slice carries the KIT SPONSOR alone, on the spec's own build order: it is the smallest step that proves the whole shape – arrival, deadline, sign, refuse, expiry – against a number that is already balanced. **It is on the world rather than in the event feed, and the spec makes that a rule**: a signed deal has to outlive every prune, `events` caps at 400 rows and a busy career burns that in a couple of seasons, so a contract announced in the feed is a contract that silently stops paying for her equipment two seasons later. ⚠ **The back-fill is empty, and unlike v29's and v31's no-ops that is not a bargain struck with a pruned log – there is genuinely nothing to reconstruct.** v18 mined surviving evidence, v28 rebuilt a split from finish indices, v31 declined to guess at a count it could not see; all three were looking at a record of things that HAD HAPPENED. An offer is a record of a DECISION, and no decision was ever taken – until this version the kit deal was not a decision at all but weather (`reviewLocalSponsor` added $1,000 or $2,000 at the season boundary and the player was never asked), so there is no earlier state that means "he signed" or "he refused". This is v26's case exactly: fabricating rows would mean fabricating decisions the player never made, which is the one thing a ledger OF decisions must never contain. ⚠ **And the cash it was receiving simply stops** – the one migration here that leaves a career materially poorer. Nothing is clawed back and every grant already banked stays banked, but the next season boundary raises a letter instead of a cheque and the parent has to sign it; the deal he can sign is worth the same figure in KIT (the shop covers her racquet, string and shoe bills up to the allowance and keeps her kit fresh) that it used to be in money – «кит вместо денег». Written defensively (an absent or non-array value is rebuilt whole) for the append-only reason v30 states. The one sub-stream the slice adds, `seed:offer:<week>`, did not exist before, so no existing stream shifts by a draw and the frozen MAIN capture (41550 / e6b0c709) is untouched by construction. This fixture is the real migration's own output on `v31.json`, the recipe every fixture since v25 uses) |

| v33 | offer `terms +covers +travelShare +seasons` (THE BRAND LADDER: a sponsorship rung stopped being one shop and became three, and **the rung says WHICH OF HER EQUIPMENT LINES the deal covers** – `local` her strings, `national` strings and frames, `global` everything plus a share of the airfare. See `SponsorTier` for the design, `ECONOMY.sponsorship` for every number, and `docs/specs/offers-and-the-inbox.md` §4.1b. The `local` gate is the domestic table it always was; the two rungs above it read the **ITF** one, which is the whole point – the owner finished a season #1 national and #13 international and only a shop in his daughter's town was writing to her. ⚠ **This one BACK-FILLS, which is the opposite of v32 a row above, and the difference is exactly the one v32's own note draws.** v32 refused to mine because an offer is a record of a DECISION and no decision had ever been taken; here a decision HAS been taken – a v32 career may be holding a signed contract this very week – and the three new fields are not a guess about what the player chose, they are the terms of the deal he already agreed to, written down. Refusing to fill them would not be modesty, it would be losing a contract. ⚠ **And the value is the OLD behaviour, not the new rung's.** Under v32 a local deal covered ALL THREE LINES (`KIT_DEAL_CATEGORIES` was rackets/stringing/shoes and the freshness cap applied to every line of `KitWear`); under v33 a local deal covers her strings alone. A back-fill of `TIER_COVERS.local` would quietly take two lines away from a contract whose letter is still in the player's inbox promising them – re-writing history in the brand's favour. `activeKitDeal` has said since the day it shipped that a deal signed under one set of numbers is honoured under those numbers for its whole life; this is that rule meeting its first real test, and `untilWeek` is left alone for the same reason. `travelShare` is 0 and `seasons` is 1 because no rung paid for travel and no deal ran past one season before this version. Written defensively (a malformed terms object is skipped, an already-filled one is left alone) for the append-only reason v30 states, which also makes it idempotent. The arrival draw stays on `seed:offer:<week>` where v32 put it – no stream is added or reordered, so the frozen MAIN capture (41550 / e6b0c709) is untouched by construction. This fixture is the real migration's own output on `v32.json`, the recipe every fixture since v25 uses) |

| v34 | world `+onRampCleared` (THE ON-RAMPS SHE HAS ALREADY CROSSED – `{itf, wta}`. An on-ramp is the bottom rung of a table, the one with no acceptance list, and its band is denominated in the table BELOW it: J30 reads her domestic best-6 against 250, W15 reads her ITF junior best-6 against 120. ⚠ **Both of those are ROLLING 52-WEEK windows, so the evidence that she once cleared the bar deletes itself.** A season spent abroad ages out every domestic result and the J30 door closes behind her; from eighteen the J rungs are shut on AGE, so no junior point can ever be earned again and W15 closes on its own a year later with nothing she could do about it. The owner, playing: «не может играть в J серии, потому что ранг в national упал» – and, on the rule: «въезд – это порог, который переходят один раз, а не условие, которое держат постоянно». Measured before the fix (`tools/j30-onramp-lock.ts`, 216 careers): **209 went through the J30 door and were shut out again, 160 of them while J60 or J300 stood OPEN**, median 53 weeks of it; and **188 had at least one week at 18+ with nothing open on either real table**. After: 0, 0 and 7 – and those 7 never cleared the W15 standard at all, which is a girl who did not make it rather than a rule eating her access. ⚠ **Acceptance lists deliberately do NOT latch**: J60/J300/W35/W100 are entry cuts read against a CURRENT ranking, because no real entry list admits you on a ranking you held two years ago. The latch guarantees a way back ONTO a table, never a place in a field. ⚠ **The back-fill is EXACT, which is rare in this file and worth the sentence.** v18 mined surviving evidence and admitted its firsts were only the earliest still-visible ones; v28 clamped a reconstruction to what the feed still reached; v29/v31/v32 refused to guess at all. Here nothing has to be guessed: `bestFinishByTier` is a HIGH-WATER MARK that is never pruned, so "has she ever finished an event on this table" is answerable for every save however long ago it happened – which is the difference between a girl keeping the access she earned and a girl being asked to earn it twice. Two weaker sources are OR-ed in for saves with no marks yet (a counting result inside the current window; the on-ramp's band met today), and `latchOnRamps` re-checks both on every tick anyway, so they only make a migrated save correct BEFORE its first tick. Written defensively and idempotently (an existing object is left alone) for the append-only reason v30 states – and `latchOnRamps` itself is defensive for a sharper version of the same rule: the migration ladder calls `recomputeKidRank` from its EARLY steps, long before this one runs, so the field genuinely is absent there. Pure state, zero draws, no sub-stream added or reordered – the frozen MAIN capture (41550 / e6b0c709) cannot move. This fixture is the real migration's own output on `v33.json`, the recipe every fixture since v25 uses) |

| v35 | world `+rngMain` (THE PERSISTED MAIN POSITION – `{s, n}`, mulberry32's register and the cumulative MAIN draw count, docs/review/proposals/P3-rng-persistence.md. Until this version the stream position was not in the save at all: every load rebuilt it by replaying the whole career – `restoreRng` ran one full `tickWeek` per elapsed week, ~1.5 ms each, on every load of every career, for ever – and the validity of that replay taxed every feature with the frozen-capture discipline (the cross-suite constant 41550 / e6b0c709 that could never move). ⚠ **The migration performs that replay for the LAST time per career and writes the answer down**: `replayMainState` is byte-identical to what `restoreRng` did – a fresh probe world on the same seed, no entries, one tick per week, valid because the per-week MAIN draw count is independent of player input – and its `{s, n}` output is stamped into the save. The two fields are REDUNDANT on purpose (`s = seed32 + n·0x6d2b79f5 mod 2³²`, mulberry32's register advances by a constant, output-independently): the pair is its own checksum, `mainStateConsistent` is the load-time verifier, and a corrupted pair routes through `recoverMainState` – the same replay, now demoted to corruption recovery – with the snapshot's `recovered: true` flag. ⚠ **The invariant regime changed with this version**: input-independence (player choices cannot re-roll the world's dice) is still law, proved pairwise A/B in the converted suites; cross-version draw-count stability is retired – the capture constant in tests/condition.test.ts B1 is a documented measurement now, updated freely by any wave that legitimately adds a MAIN draw. This fixture is the real migration's own output on `v34.json`, the recipe every fixture since v25 uses: seed golden-v27 at week 60 lands on `{s: 1815598547, n: 47942}` – 60 × (3 base + 4×199 drift) + 2 sponsor hits, the arithmetic of the tick's own budget – and that exact pair is the frozen tripwire in tests/migrations.test.ts that catches any future change silently drifting the migration replay) |

For **v0–v5** the migration regenerates the world systems (cohort/season) deterministically from the
seed, so those fixtures are the authentic minimal historical shapes. For **v6–v7** the `cohort` /
`season` / `events` arrays are trimmed to a couple of representative entries (the migration never
regenerates a v6+ world, so their contents are exercised as *shape*, not size) to keep the fixtures
readable.

When you add a new fixture, keep it small but structurally faithful to that exact schema version.
